To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) distance increases the bargaining costs of the headquarter-sidiary relationship, 2) relationship atmosphere reduces both types of costs, 3) formalization and centralization reduce information costs and 4) social integration increases the bargaining costs in the headquater-subsidiary relation.

(i) relationship atmosphere is a key factor that can reduce organizing costs, and (ii) the effects of coordination mechanisms and distance on organizing costs vary, and depend on other contextual factors.

(1) the relationship atmosphere between headquarters and subsidiaries is the most important determinant of the level of organizing cost, and (2) the effects of distance and coordination mechanisms depend on the type of costs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how MNC subsidiaries experience interactions with headquarters.
the costs of organizing the headquarter-subidiary relationship and the factors that affect such costs.
how the headquarter-subidiary relationship is experienced from the subsidiary's perspective, and how the experience of organizing costs is affected by different contextual factors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the atmosphere in the relationship is the most important factor for the level of organizing cost.
distance and atmosphere influence organizing costs in the relationship between the headquarters and the subsidiaries in MNCs, and that coordination mechanisms have a more complex effect.
atmosphere is a key factor in the headquarter-subidiary relationship, whereas other factors are more or less important depending on the type of costs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
atmosphere, distance, centralization, formalization and social integration are important factors that influence the level of interaction between subsidiaries and corporate headquarters in MNCs.
the more the atmosphere between headquarters and subsidiaries is characterized by trust, respect, and mutual support, the lower the organizing costs.

a subsidiary's distance from the corporate headquarters, as well as the subsidiary's relationship atmosphere with the headquarters, is an important predictor of the level of organizing cost experienced in the subsidiary-headquarter relationship.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the relationship between the subsidiary and headquarters can be improved by reducing both types of organizing cost.
the organizing costs in the headquarters-subidiary relationship are not solely determined by the characteristics of the relationship, but also by the characteristics of corporate headquarters.
MNCs should be aware of the costs of interactions with corporate headquarters and should take actions to minimize these costs.
